clue.text: Withdraw from contract

definitions.meaning: to withdraw is to draw back or recoil, as from something unpleasant
to contract is to get smaller

explanation.definitionFit: Shrinking means both recoiling in fear and becoming smaller, so the one verb covers each sense.

clue.text: Unwelcome dependant causes irritation in unpaid host

indicators.note: in means the irritation goes inside the unpaid host

parts.note: Hon, short for honorary, describes an unpaid officer such as an honorary host
anger is irritation

explanation.surface: A freeloader annoys a host who gets nothing for his trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Hon., for honorary, marks an unpaid post, so the unpaid host gives HON.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanger-on is a sycophantic follower who attaches themselves to someone for gain.

clue.text: One rising City business providing security for frozen assets

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the letters read upwards

parts.note: EC is the postcode area for the City of London
a house is a business firm, as in a fashion house

explanation.surface: A City firm on the up offers protection for frozen funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frozen assets' sounds financial, as City and business encourage; it means ice kept cold.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice house was a building, often underground, for keeping winter ice stored through summer.

clue.text: It is mounted below the gear to keep watch for flier

indicators.note: below places the mounted word under the gear in this down entry

parts.note: kit is gear or equipment

indicators.note: is mounted in a down entry means the word climbs, reading upward

parts.note: to wake is to keep a vigil or watch

explanation.surface: Someone climbs up below the equipment to keep an eye out for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A kittiwake is a seabird, a kind of gull, and any bird is a flier.

clue.text: Seditious leader in grip of chief executioner

indicators.note: one piece held in the grip of another sits inside it

parts.note: a headman is a chief of a tribe or village

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so take the first of seditious

explanation.surface: A rebel ringleader falls into the hands of the chief executioner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seditious leader' sounds like a rebel chief, but it is just the letter S; 'chief executioner' looks like one title, yet 'chief' is wordplay and 'executioner' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A headsman was the official who beheaded condemned prisoners, an executioner by axe.

clue.text: A horse trained to produce classical racers

indicators.note: produce means the letters are worked into something new

explanation.surface: A racehorse is trained to produce champions of the classic races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classical' suggests the Classics of British flat racing, but these racers come from Aesop's fable; 'trained' looks like the signal but is part of the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In Aesop's ancient fable a speedy animal loses a race to a slow one, so the pair are racers from antiquity.

clue.text: Daughter joined in marriage perhaps, having flirted

parts.note: allied means joined, marriage being one way families are allied

explanation.surface: A daughter got married after some flirting.
explanation.definitionFit: To dally is to toy amorously, to trifle with someone's affections.

clue.text: Part of the bill for service with meals

definitions.text: Part of the bill for service with meals

parts.words: Part of the bill for service with meals
parts.note: reads like a restaurant's service charge, but means the part of a bird's beak, or a jaw, used when eating

explanation.definitionFit: The upper or lower part of a bird's beak is called this, and it is the jaw that works at mealtimes.

clue.text: Teachers taking form in this shortly

parts.note: the NUT is the National Union of Teachers
the Shell is a form, a school class, at some English public schools

explanation.surface: Teachers take over a class, put briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT was Britain's National Union of Teachers; at some English schools the Shell is a form between years. 'in this shortly' alludes to the idiom 'in a ___', meaning briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting something in a few words is the idiom of a tiny case of a nut, meaning concisely.

clue.text: Old man perhaps — a wise old man, about a hundred

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the wise old man goes round the hundred

parts.note: Nestor was the aged, wise counsellor of the Greeks in Homer
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Someone's grandfather is described as a wise old man of nearly a hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: NESTOR is the Greek elder in the Iliad, whose name stands for any wise old man.
explanation.definitionFit: An old man, a father or forebear, is an example of a forefather in one's family line.

clue.text: Space traveller in level orbit at last

parts.note: plane means flat or level

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of orbit

explanation.surface: A spacecraft travels in a flat orbit, finally.
explanation.definitionFit: A world such as Mars journeys endlessly round its sun, so it is a wanderer through space.

clue.text: She gets a pass from a fighter in the ring

definitions.meaning: a woman, here one with a girl's name

definitions.text: a pass from a fighter in the ring
definitions.meaning: a bullfighter's slow sweep of the cape past the charging bull, made in the bullring

explanation.definitionFit: Veronica is a woman's name and also the matador's classic cape pass, named after the saint who wiped Christ's face with a cloth.

clue.text: Polish, but like another tongue in utterance

indicators.note: in utterance means as the words are spoken, signalling a sound-alike

parts.note: Finnish describes something in the language of Finland

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the Polish language is really like another tongue when spoken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' tempts as the nationality, but it is the verb meaning to give a final gloss; the language of Finland sounds the same when said.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish furniture is to give it its final surface treatment, a last coat or glaze.

clue.text: One thoroughfare taken along with another, for example

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
and means along with
a means one
Rd, short for road, is another thoroughfare

explanation.surface: One street is joined to another, as an illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in a different order from the clue: the street, then AND, then the 'One', then the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A model to be copied or measured against is a benchmark, an example others follow.

clue.text: Harvest fruit comes up again

parts.note: to reap is to harvest
pears are fruit

explanation.surface: Each harvest the fruit returns.
explanation.definitionFit: To come up again is to show up a second time, return into view.

clue.text: Stake transfixing Transylvanian terror

indicators.note: the answer runs through the following words, pinned across them as a stake would be

explanation.surface: A wooden stake is driven through a Transylvanian monster, a vampire.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across the end of Transylvanian and the start of terror.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the opening stake each player puts in the pot before the deal is the ante, a wager.

clue.text: Frightening gangster procuring weapons

parts.note: Al Capone is the crossword's stock gangster
arming is acquiring weapons

explanation.surface: A scary mobster is stocking up on guns.
explanation.definitionFit: Something frightening causes fear and worry, which is what alarm means.

clue.text: Refuse to reduce the volume

definitions.meaning: to refuse is to reject or decline an offer
to lower the sound on a radio by moving the dial

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both declining a request and lowering the setting of a dial.

clue.text: Gem not right for ring

indicators.note: not here means leave out the letter for right

parts.note: a pearl is a gem from an oyster

explanation.surface: A precious stone that is not quite right for an engagement ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring' looks like the jewellery the gem goes into, but it is the verb or noun for bells sounding.
explanation.definitionFit: A peal is a loud ringing of a set of bells.

clue.text: It's urgent — requiring use of club in 22?

definitions.meaning: an urgent matter demands immediate attention
the club hidden at the start of the answer to 22 is the iron, here the household appliance used on clothes

explanation.walkthrough: A golf club is an iron, and the 22 answer begins with those letters; the domestic sense is smoothing clothes with a hot iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing means both urgent and the act of ironing garments flat.

clue.text: Give ground with rage in upset

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and remade

explanation.surface: Someone concedes territory angrily while distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give ground' reads as one phrase meaning retreat, but 'ground' is the anagram signal working on GIVE and RAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To aggrieve someone is to distress or wrong them, to cause them grievance.

clue.text: Carefree bride on a jaunt

indicators.note: a jaunt is a trip about the place, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A carefree bride sets off on a pleasure trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair means jaunty, lighthearted and self-assured.

clue.text: Mounted foray first described by Evelyn, say

indicators.note: mounted in a down entry means the word is read climbing upward

parts.note: a raid is a foray
1st, with the figure written as the letter I

explanation.surface: A cavalry raid was first recorded by the seventeenth-century writer Evelyn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted foray' suggests a cavalry raid, but 'Mounted' only turns RAID upward; 1ST becomes IST. John Evelyn kept a famous seventeenth-century diary.
explanation.definitionFit: John Evelyn is famed for his daily journal of life in Restoration England, an example of a chronicler of his days.

clue.text: Fugitive lacking heart in airport departure area

indicators.note: lacking heart means the middle letter of the word for fugitive is dropped

parts.note: a runaway is a fugitive

explanation.surface: A heartless fugitive is caught in the departure area of an airport.
explanation.walkthrough: The fugitive word has seven letters; removing its central A leaves the strip planes take off from.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstrip from which aircraft take off is the part of an airport they depart from.

clue.text: Attempt to contain a nuisance by design of sewer

indicators.note: to contain means the word for attempt goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a try is an attempt
a pest is a nuisance

explanation.surface: Someone tries to deal with a rat in the drains with a new design of sewer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sewer' reads as a drain, but it is one who sews: an embroiderer's design.
explanation.definitionFit: A woven or embroidered wall hanging is the patterned work of someone stitching with a needle.

clue.text: Incongruous architectural style gets royal introduction

indicators.note: an introduction here means the royal letter is put into the style

parts.note: Ionic is one of the classical orders of Greek architecture
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: An odd building style gains a royal opening ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduction' suggests a presentation at court, but it means putting R inside the column style.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ironic is incongruous: the outcome is at odds with what was expected.

clue.text: Pictures commonly disapproved of in house replaced

indicators.note: in places the dialect word inside the rearranged house
replaced means the letters of the word for house are put back in a new order

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house
agin is a colloquial form of against, so 'I'm agin it' means I disapprove

explanation.surface: Paintings that ordinary people disliked in a home were swapped for others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pictures' looks like a plural noun but is the verb. A semi is a British semi-detached house; 'replaced' gives IMES, and the dialect 'agin' (as in 'I'm agin it') is the disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: To picture something is to form a mental image of it, to visualise.

clue.text: A case of possession?

parts.note: reads like a demonic possession or legal case, but means the grammatical case that shows ownership

explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, the case marking possession, as in Latin or English 's, has this name.

clue.text: Endorsed slight alteration in design

indicators.note: a slight alteration rearranges the letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A design was approved after a minor change.
explanation.definitionFit: Endorsing a cheque means writing one's name on it, putting a signature there.
